Faculty: Dr. Mohanababu Ch


Finance Elective


Course Name: Advanced Managerial Accounting


CODE: CUFM2350
 
Credits:  3+0+1
Course Objectives: 
●
To equip the students with various concepts, tools and techniques
Cost and Management accounting.
●
To provide thorough understanding and techniques of financial
statements analysis.
●
To provide an understanding of methods of cost accounting and its
relevance in management decision making.


Course Outcomes:
On successful completion
of this course, students will be able to:
●
Critically analyze and improve the operations of organisations
through the application of management accounting techniques;
●
Read, interpret and analyze financial statements; combine
financial analysis with other information to assess the financial performance
and position of a company;
●
Interpret and analyze the financial statements by using the
techniques of financial statement analysis for managerial decision-making;
●
Apply relevant costing methods to analyze specific business
issues.
●
Develop (plan and forecast) budgets for difference business.
●

Course Syllabus
Module: I Concept of
Management Accounting
Concept; Tools of
Management Accounting; Difference between Financial Accounting, Cost Accounting
& Management Accounting, and their Scopes; Role of Management Accountant in
Decision Making
 
Module: II Financial
Performance Analysis
Corporate Financial
Statements: Income Statement and Balance Sheet, concepts of triple balance
sheet and The integrated report framework
Financial Statement
Analysis: Common Size Statements, Comparative Analysis, Trend Analysis,
Financial Ratio Analysis, Inter-firm and intra-firm comparison.
 
Module: III
Standard Costing and CVP Analysis
Standard Costing and
Variance analysis: Concept of Standard Cost and Standard Costing, Types of
Variance (Material Variance and Labour Variance); Activity Based Costing 
CVP Analysis and CVP
Application in decision making; 
 
Module: IV Budgetary
Control 
Budget, Budgeting,
Classification of Budget: Cash Budget, Fixed Budget and Flexible Budget,
Zero-Base Budgeting, Responsibility Accounting; 
 
Books Recommended:
1.Horngren, Foster &
Dater - Cost Accounting: A Managerial Emphasis     (Pearson)
2.M.N. Arora – Cost and
Management Accounting Theory and Problems Vikash
3.Khan and Jain-
Management Accounting-TMH
 
Project Topics


Module I: Concept of Management
Accounting

  1. Role of Management Accounting in Strategic
    Decision-Making: A Study of Selected Companies
  2. Comparative Analysis of Financial
    Accounting, Cost Accounting, and Management Accounting in Business
    Organizations
  3. Impact of Management Accounting
    Information on Business Performance
  4. Changing Role of Management Accountants in
    the Digital Business Environment
  5. Management Accounting Tools and Their
    Application in Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)
Module II: Financial Performance
Analysis

  1. Financial Performance Analysis of a Listed
    Company Using Ratio Analysis
  2. Comparative Financial Statement Analysis
    of Two Companies in the Same Industry
  3. Trend Analysis of Financial Performance: A
    Five-Year Study of a Manufacturing Company
  4. Common-Size Financial Statement Analysis
    as a Tool for Performance Evaluation
  5. Integrated Reporting Framework and
    Corporate Performance: An Empirical Study
  6. Triple Balance Sheet Approach and
    Sustainable Business Performance: A Case Study
Module III: Standard Costing and CVP
Analysis

  1. Application of Standard Costing and
    Variance Analysis in Manufacturing Industries
  2. Material and Labour Variance Analysis for
    Cost Control: A Case Study
  3. Activity-Based Costing (ABC) versus
    Traditional Costing: A Comparative Study
  4. Cost-Volume-Profit (CVP) Analysis in
    Profit Planning and Decision Making
  5. Break-Even Analysis and Its Role in
    Pricing Decisions: An Industry-Based Study
Module IV: Budgetary Control

  1. Effectiveness of Budgetary Control Systems
    in Business Organizations
  2. Flexible Budgeting versus Fixed Budgeting:
    A Comparative Analysis
  3. Zero-Based Budgeting as a Tool for Cost
    Reduction and Resource Allocation
  4. Responsibility Accounting and Performance
    Evaluation: A Case Study of a Corporate Organization     Top
    of Form
